entities.summary: Jean Simon Pictet was a Swiss citizen, jurist, legal practitioner working in international humanitarian law. First as a secretary-jurist, and then as a senior executive and Vice-President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), Pictet was instrumental in drafting the 1949 Geneva Conventions for the protection of victims of war, their Commentaries, and negotiating the 1977 Additional Protocols. He also proposed the Red Cross Movement’s seven Fundamental Principles, which were adopted at Vienna in 1965: Humanity, Impartiality, Neutrality, Independence, Voluntary Service, Unity and Universality.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pictet's work on the Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols has had a profound impact on international humanitarian law, shaping the protection of victims of war and influencing the development of human rights. His proposal of the Red Cross Movement's seven Fundamental Principles continues to guide the organization's mission.
